I don't speak English that well, but when I look at this, if you look -- just read it in English. And I would like it to be reinterpreted into French, that it be reinterpreted. I would like that sentence to be reinterpreted, the answer. All right, continue, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, who in the HVO took prisoners out to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that, who it was exactly, by name and post, who did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you hear it from?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We would ask for a private or closed session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, closed session. (Closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Open session)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could just have this particular video marked as an exhibit, and if we could dim the lights and play it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be 515.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could ask the translator to translate as we go through?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There are subtitles on the film and it is hard to hear it here. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier, the fall of Srbrenica on the 16th of April was the culmination of a series of Bosnian Serb offensives that had started in April of 1993; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot claim that. I was not in contact with the command of the army of Republika Srpska. Srbrenica is quite far away from us. It is a 300- or 200-kilometre distance, so I cannot say anything about Srbrenica except for what the video we have all seen here says for itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me show you a map, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 516.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier, the source of the information that's on this map are UNPROFOR situation maps as well as the United Nations Commission of Experts report. Let's go through this map. Beginning in the early part of February, the dates designated don't necessarily say that it's the end of the battle, but the purple arrows reflect the direction of Bosnian Serb attacks. It's true, is it not, that an offensive began in Brcko on the 3rd of February, 1993, where the VRS attacked ABiH positions or Armija positions in Brcko; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really cannot claim that. When the army of the Republika Srpska, in this area of Tuzla, in the Sarajevo area and other areas further off from Central Bosnia, when that was attacked, if this is a document, an international document, by international organisations, and they claim that it is so, I have no reason to say that it isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the Central Bosnian Operative Zone had brigades in Sarajevo, didn't they? I think we talked about that last week.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We had an HVO brigade in Sarajevo which was active within the composition of the 1st Corps of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on approximately the 17th or thereabouts, the 17th of February of 1993, the shelling of Sarajevo by the Bosnian Serbs commenced in earnest, not only Sarajevo but the area around Mostar and Kojnic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot claim this because I don't recall, but when we come to the HVO brigade in Sarajevo, we did not obtain from that brigade any operational reports as to what was going on in the zone under its control on the defence line towards the Republika Srpska, so that brigade belonged to the command of the Operative Zone organisationally speaking but it was under the command of the command of the 1st Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In and around the 3rd of March, is it not true that the shelling of Sarajevo commenced again by the Bosnian Serbs and also the beginning of the provinces, the enclaves, in eastern Bosnia, that is Cerska -- Cerska, Srbrenica and Zepa, the attacks on those enclaves began.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say whether any of these facts are correct because I don't know when the army attacked the units of the Bosnia and Herzegovina army around Sarajevo, in Srbrenica, and the other places mentioned by you. According to my knowledge, my personal knowledge, on the attacks of the BH army in the area of Sarajevo and the area around Tuzla and Srbrenica with the units of the Republika Srpska army, usually we learnt about this from the media, the public media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, turn down to the next, in Sarajevo where the shelling began in earnest of Sarajevo on the 17th of March 1993, and let's go a couple of days to the 21st of March. Did you not learn from your brigades down there that on the 20th and 21st of March that the Bosnian Serb army fired approximately 3.000 shells on both of those days into Sarajevo? Did you learn that from your brigades?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness, on three, four or five accounts, said that he did not have any knowledge on what happened outside the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. The Prosecutor is taking him through this document and he has answered on each count he does not know what happened. I don't see the purpose of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, would you define your objective more clearly, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The objective is simple, Mr. President. This witness testified that this attack on the 16th of April was a surprise attack by the Bosnian Muslims. In a relatively close area to Central Bosnia, various offensives, various significant offensives were taking place by the army of, by the Bosnian Serb army against the Bosnian Muslims, beginning with the 3rd of February in Brcko. It continued on the 17th of February in Sarajevo and Mostar and Konjic. After a brief lull it began again in Sarajevo and the invasion into Srpska took place. Later on in March, Your Honour, the shelling of Sarajevo began in earnest, focusing on the days I just discussed, the 20th and 21st of March, very well-known days, very well-known days in the conflict in the former Yugoslavia, in excess of 3.000 shells fell on Sarajevo. Now, while this is going on, the enclaves are being invaded, and we heard General Morillon testifying as to what was happening in Srebrenica, as well as the enclaves at Srpska and Zepce were under siege. What was happening in all these fronts, all the fronts that are on this map, was that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was under serious, serious attack. And given the fact they were under attack and losing these battles, it defies any logic they would open up a second front against the Bosnian Croats when they were getting annihilated and destroyed in these other locales. It would, in essence, to use a simple term, be cutting their own throat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Prosecutor has to find what he is looking for. You said that it defied all logic. You had an official, an important position. It's true that very often you do seem to know nothing. Since the Prosecutor has explained his question, do you still give us the same answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, if I wanted at this point to claim that it was so, I would have to recall all the dates and say it was so, and this would not be the objective or realistic for me; so for these dates and concrete activities I'm afraid I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: How many kilometres is Sarajevo from Vitez and Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sarajevo is 80 kilometres away from Vitez and Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Continue, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree, Brigadier, that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the army, was being attacked on numerous fronts by the Bosnian Serb army between February and April of 1993, and they were losing; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot bear this out. If these facts are exact, then it is obvious that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina on those dates was attacked by the army of, the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the same time, Brigadier, that you say that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina engaged in a surprise attack on the 16th of April, 1993, Srebrenica was falling, as we just heard on the tape; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to what I saw on the tape, it is exact that Srebrenica was falling. But, Mr. President, in my testimony about the 16th, the attack on the 16th, I did not say I was attacked by the forces of the 1st Corps or the 2nd Corps forces; but we were attacked by the forces of the 3rd Corps from the Zenica area, from the Zenica area. We were with them, in conflict with them, and we were fighting a war against them, not in Vitez with the forces of the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, just like the HVO, was a unitary command; wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, that is so. But let me add that in those particular days, in our operative reports, the reports that we received, the Serbs, the army of the Republika Srpska, attacked the HVO area in Zepce. So the activities of the army of the Republika Srpska probably had some of their own plans, and I cannot say what the army of the Republika Srpska had at its objective.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as General Petkovic was running the HVO, General Halilovic, the person we saw surrendering to the Bosnian Serbs on the tape, he was the general of the entire army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise, but General Halilovic was the commander of the units of the Bosnia-Herzegovina army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I said, we agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could give another document to Your Honours, and this is a UN Security Council resolution in French and in English. Mr. President, I don't intend to read this entire document, it is in French and English, it is a UN security resolution of the 16th of April, 1993, declaring the Srebrenica enclave a safe area. But I do think that several lines in this item does bear some reference during this discourse.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 517, 517A for the French version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just with regard to the first page, this is resolution 819 of 16 April, 1993, "The Security Council, after reaffirming various resolutions, takes note that the International Court of Justice, in its order of 8 April, 1993, in the case concerning the application of the convention on the prevention and punishment of the crime of genocide, Bosnia-Herzegovina versus Yugoslavia, Serbia and Montenegro unanimously indicated as to the provisional measure that the government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Serbia and Montenegro should immediately, in pursuance of its undertaking in the convention of the prevention and punishment of the crime of genocide of 9 December, 1948, take all measures within its power to prevent the commission of the crime of genocide." We will skip three paragraphs. The paragraph starting with "Concerned by the pattern of hostilities by Bosnian Serb power military units against towns and villages in Eastern Bosnia in this region, reaffirming that any taking or acquisition of territory by threat or use of force, including through the practice of ethnic cleansing, is unlawful and unacceptable. Deeply alarmed at the information provided by the Secretary-General to the Security Council on 16 April, 1993 on the rapid deterioration of the situation in Srebrenica and its surrounding areas, as a result of the continued deliberate armed attacks and shelling of the innocent civilian population by Bosnian Serb paramilitary units." We will skip two paragraphs. "Aware that a tragic humanitarian emergency has already developed in Srebrenica and its surrounding areas as a direct consequence of the brutal actions of the Bosnian Serb paramilitary units forcing the large scale displacement of civilians, in particular women, children and the elderly." Go to the demands, "Demands that all parties and others concerned treat Srebrenica and surrounding areas as a safe area which should be free from any armed attack or other hostile act. 2. Demands also to the effect, the immediate cessation of armed attacks by Bosnian Serb paramilitary units against Srebrenica and their immediate withdrawal of the areas around Srebrenica." Down to the bottom of the page, 6, "Condemns and rejects the deliberate actions of the Bosnian Serb party to force the evacuation of the civilian population from Srebrenica and its surrounding areas, as well as from other parts of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina as part of the overall abhorrent campaign of ethnic cleansing. 9. Urges the Secretary-General and the United Nations High Commissioner of Refugees to use all resources at their disposal in the scope of the relevant resolutions of the council to reinforce the existing humanitarian operations in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in particular Srebrenica and its surroundings." And the last one we will read is 11. "Further request the Secretary-General, in consultation with UNHCR and UNPROFOR, to arrange or the safe transport of wounded and ill civilians from Srebrenica and surrounding areas and urgently report thereon to the council." That, of course, Mr. President is an official document of the UN filed on the 16th of April 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Ask your question, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, would it be fair to say, Brigadier, based on what you heard and what you have seen today, Srebrenica was a humanitarian and military disaster for the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From what we saw on the film, we saw that the population had suffered greatly and that it was truly an act which was very difficult for the people living in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, well, we won't get into -- based on what you've seen and based on what you heard, you still maintain, sir, that it was the Bosnian Muslims or the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina who attacked the HVO on the morning of the 16th of April 1993? Is that still your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is part of my testimony, on the basis of what I experienced on the 16th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn to just another document, if you will.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do we have an easel here? Can we bring in an easel? I don't know what time, Mr. President, you're going to break. I have a document that I would like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: On the same subject?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, on the same subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If my colleague agrees. All right, distribute the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's a map, Mr. President, but we can distribute, Defence Exhibit 401, 402 and 403. Defence Exhibit 401, 402 and 403, while we're setting up the map. I think in a very brief period of time, Mr. President, I think I can complete this area of discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go ahead. The interpreters will work a few more minutes, I'm sure. Thank you. Mr. Dubuisson, if we can also have this map marked and put on the ELMO, marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The map is 518.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier, while the usher is putting the map up on the board, previously during your direct testimony you gave us some orders from, or some requests from the 8th of January, 5th of February of 1993, and the 1st of July of 1992. And I'm referring to, in series, Exhibits 401, 402 and 403. These are requests to be able to transit HVO areas by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, to travel with ammunition, et cetera; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier, the resupply of the Bosnian Herzegovinins, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, had to come through either Croatia or an area controlled by the HVO; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the map that is before us, that is, the map 518, and I took the liberty of writing in red on that map the supply lines coming from the Dalmatian coasts. My question for you, Brigadier, is: Do you agree that those are the major supply lines that would go from the Dalmatian coasts up into Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Counsel, I advise you to come over and take a look at the map. I apologise for asking the question without giving that courtesy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I approach the map, as well, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that they are, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all those areas, those particular supply routes, all transit through Croatia and through HVO controlled area, one obviously going through Prozor and the other going, for instance, through Jablanica; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. This route passes by the following places; Tomislavgrad, where the HVO was present; through Prozor, where the army and the HVO were there, the HVO was dominant; it passes through Gornji Vakuf, where we have the army and the HVO, from Gornji Vakuf along the length of 40 kilometres, it passes through an area controlled by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; and further on from there, Novi Travnik. It moves across the territory of Vitez municipality, where we have units of the HVO and the BH army. So, if we go from Vitez towards Zenica, towards Zenica, from Kaonik onwards, from Lasva, that is to the say, this territory was controlled by the BH army units. As far as the supply line passing through Central Bosnia from Split, for example, to Zenica, it passed through a territory which was controlled both by the units of the HVO and the Bosnian BH army. And for that reason, this type of communication was established, so that when we would take supplies, we would ask the army to ensure safe passage through these areas mentioned a moment ago where the army had its checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree with me, Brigadier, these are the life lines for Central Bosnia; isn't that so? These are the routes that basically are used to resupply Central Bosnia; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were routes for supplying Central Bosnia and the HVO, under its own organisation with its own resources, participated in building and preparing the roads for the forthcoming winter period, so that the supplies of the needs of the army and food should be effective and efficient as possible. Because part of the roads pass through mountainous ground, which is very difficult under winter conditions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina attacked the HVO, the first response of the HVO and the HV would be to cut those supply lines to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That can be stated in that way and thought to be like that, but the attack was because of the supply routes. The BH army attacked in order to gain control of the supply lines, fully gain control of the supply lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Brigadier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I've concluded this area and we will move into another area tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Tomorrow morning we will resume at 10.00. Court is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
